title: min_quote_out hardcoded to 0 disables DeepBook's slippage guard, so the keeper-supplied current_price gate is the only correctness check on swap output
description: execute_trigger calls `pool::swap_exact_base_for_quote(pool, base_in, deep_in, 0, clock, ctx)` with `min_quote_out = 0`. DeepBook's pool.move declares `EMinimumQuantityOutNotMet: u64 = 12` precisely to give callers a slippage floor, and a `min_quote_out = 0` setting unconditionally disables that protection. The contract.md does document this as a deliberate decision (`min_quote_out = 0` because the keeper's `current_price` gate is the trigger-side correctness check), but the trigger gate only ve

recommendation: Two non-mutually-exclusive options. (1) Add an optional owner-configured `min_quote_out_bps_of_deposit: Option<u64>` field to Vault that, when Some, computes `min_quote_out = (deposit_amount * bps) / 10_000` at execute_trigger time and forwards it to swap_exact_base_for_quote. This gives owners a protocol-level slippage floor independent of the keeper. (2) At minimum, add an `assert!(quote_out_amount > 0, EZeroQuoteOut)` after the swap returns, which catches the degenerate case of a fully empty book — better than silently accepting a zero-value Coin<Quote> and marking the vault triggered. Either approach should be paired with a test that fires the trigger against a fixture pool with insufficient depth and asserts the abort path.

title: create_vault accepts (None, None) TP/SL configuration silently, producing a vault that can never fire and is only drainable via withdraw
description: create_vault<T> takes `tp_price: Option<u64>` and `sl_price: Option<u64>` and constructs the Vault unconditionally — there is no `assert!(tp_price.is_some() || sl_price.is_some(), EInvalidTriggerConfig)` guard. The contract.md explicitly flagged this as 'Optional defense-in-depth (not required for AC compliance)' with an `EInvalidTriggerConfig: u64 = 1004` constant proposed but the implementer chose to omit it. The omission means: a caller who passes `tp_price = none, sl_price = none` succeeds,

recommendation: Implement the optional `EInvalidTriggerConfig: u64 = 1004` constant suggested by contract.md and add `assert!(tp_price.is_some() || sl_price.is_some(), EInvalidTriggerConfig);` at the top of create_vault, before any object construction. This produces an immediate, actionable abort at the misconfiguration point rather than at fire time. Add a unit test that calls create_vault with (None, None) and asserts the EInvalidTriggerConfig abort. title: TP and SL bounds are not validated for ordering coherence; a vault with tp_price <= sl_price always satisfies both conditions
description: create_vault accepts arbitrary `tp_price: Option<u64>` and `sl_price: Option<u64>` with no relational constraint. A coherent TP/SL configuration has `tp_price > sl_price` (take profit on upside, stop loss on downside). The contract performs no such check, so a user (or a malicious frontend) can create a vault with, e.g., `tp_price = some(1)` and `sl_price = some(10)`. recommendation: Two complementary fixes. title: Error constants do not use Move 2024 #[error] attribute, foregoing improved CLI/explorer abort diagnostics
description: The three named error codes are declared as bare `const ENotOwner: u64 = 1001;`, `const EVaultTriggered: u64 = 1002;`, `const ETriggerConditionNotMet: u64 = 1003;`. Move 2024 supports clever-error attributes per `.move-book-docs/reference/abort-and-assert/clever-errors.md` and `.move-book-docs/book/guides/better-error-handling.md`: declaring a constant as `#[error] const ENotOwner: vector<u8> = b"Caller is not the vault owner";` lets the runtime surface the human-readable message in CLI output,
impact: The three named error codes are declared as bare `const ENotOwner: u64 = 1001;`, `const EVaultTriggered: u64 = 1002;`, `const ETriggerConditionNotMet: u64 = 1003;`. Move 2024 supports clever-error att
recommendation: Migrate the three error constants to the Move 2024 `#[error]` attribute form, e.g.: `#[error] const ENotOwner: vector<u8> = b"Caller is not the vault owner";`. This composes cleanly with the existing `expected_failure(abort_code = ::tpsl_vault::tpsl_vault::ENotOwner)` test annotations (the abort_code identifier path is unchanged) while giving the keeper, the UI, and any CLI consumer a free human-readable diagnostic. Verify after the change that `sui move test -e localnet` still reports 7/7 PASS — the test annotations should not need updating.
